🇲🇽🏭 <u>Heavy Truck Exports Up 144.6% in September</u>

Mexico shipped 12,707 buses, trucks and tractor-trailers abroad in September, up from 5,196 a year earlier, according to ANPACT, the industry association. That is the biggest jump of 2026. Production rose 121%, to 15,181 units. January–September exports reached 98,394 units, up 12%. Tariffs or not, North America's freight still rides on Mexican-built trucks.

🇲🇽🌎 "Within the framework of our Constitution... territorial integrity, respect for sovereignty, mutual trust and coordination without subordination." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 9, 2026 Sheinbaum said she gave these numbers to business leaders and US Ambassador Ronald Johnson at Palacio Nacional on Thursday. Irregular border crossings are down 98%, and fentanyl seizures in the US are down 75% because of operations on the Mexican side. There are "mirror operations" since Trump sent the US Army to the border, and some 94 major drug bosses have been sent to the US. The cooperation runs under Mexico's Constitution and the National Security Law. What Mexico wants now is for the US to lower its tariffs on cars and steel.

🔥🇲🇽 "How is he going to talk about democracy? The one who committed electoral fraud?" — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 9, 2026 Asked about former presidents Zedillo, Calderón, Salinas and Fox speaking out against the 4T, Sheinbaum laid out the record. Fox reached power in 2000 with Zedillo's help and promised democracy. Four years later came the desafuero, an invented crime used to try to keep López Obrador, then Mexico City's head of government, off the 2006 ballot, until mass protests forced Fox to back down. Then came the 2006 electoral fraud. "How is Calderón going to talk about democracy if he came to power with electoral fraud? How is Salinas?" She said it matters to remember, because an 18-year-old today was born under Calderón.

🇲🇽⚖️ "It is not rhetoric, it is principles... A people without memory has no compass." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 9, 2026 A Revista Zócalo reporter said critics call her talk of sovereignty and independence a rhetorical device against Trump's threats. Sheinbaum answered that Mexico faced threats from foreign powers in the 19th and 20th centuries, that the neoliberal period opened the door to economic policy being set from abroad, and that the Calderón years opened it to US agencies operating freely on Mexican territory. The president has to keep that principle present "so that the people of Mexico have the memory of what our independence and our sovereignty have cost us." She added that 42 million people now receive a well-being program directly.

text: 🇲🇽🏭 "Google, Meta... they themselves are very interested in production of these electronics continuing in Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 9, 2026 US Census Bureau data cited at the briefing put Mexico's exports to the United States at a record $419 billion. Sheinbaum said the growth comes from electronics and products tied to artificial intelligence, as data centers and US power generation expand. Plants of Mexican and foreign companies are growing in Mexico. "As we know, President Trump is worried about the deficit," she said, but the big platform companies driving the AI boom want the production to stay. INEGI data released today also show heavy-vehicle production recovering.

🇲🇽🏭 "When construction grows, the whole economy grows." "The second half will be much better than the first half of this year, and next year much better." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 9, 2026 As of September 30, IMSS registered more than 22 million formal jobs, the highest since records began, and over 87% are permanent. Sheinbaum credited public works, mixed public-private projects and housing: social housing through Vivienda para el Bienestar plus Infonavit mortgage credits adds up to more than 300 billion pesos of investment a year, a target being met this year. A Latinobarómetro survey this week found 59% of Mexicans expect their personal or family economic situation to improve in the next 12 months.

🇲🇽✊ "It is a great advantage to be in IMSS-Bienestar." "States without IMSS-Bienestar have practically the same consultations in 2023 and 2026, and in those in IMSS-Bienestar, the number of consultations increased 50%." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 9, 2026 Joining the federal health system is voluntary, and any state that doesn't want to has the right not to. Shared resources and services are what make the difference, she said. Today she starts a tour of IMSS-Bienestar hospitals in the 24 states that joined, beginning in Hidalgo and the State of Mexico, to meet every hospital director, hear what is missing and push the digitization of medical records.

🇲🇽⚖️ "It is a decree, it is mandatory. It is not whether they want to or not." "We cannot allow platforms to be unsafe spaces for children and adolescents." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 9, 2026 Legal Counsel Luisa María Alcalde presented the decree. Platforms may not expose minors to hate speech, violent extremism, sexual abuse, suicide or self-harm, eating disorders, school violence, cyberbullying or explicit material. They must remove such accounts at once, classify content by age, make the most protective settings the default, give parents supervision tools and keep a 24/7 contact point for investigators. It is due in the official gazette by Wednesday. There are no sanctions for now: "If the platforms don't comply, then we'll make it a law with its sanctions."
